\subsection{Free Carrier Absorption}

Once electrons are promoted to the conduction band, they behave as quasi free carriers. The laser field accelerates them, and they drift in opposition to the electrical field $\vec{E}$~\cite{mao2004}. One might expect these carriers to keep absorbing photons and gaining energy directly. However, single photon absorption by an isolated free electron is forbidden, because it cannot simultaneously satisfy conservation of energy and conservation of momentum.

For the absorption of a photon $(\omega_0,\vec{k}_{\text{ph}})$ by an electron with initial wave vector $\vec{k}_i$ moving to a final state with wave vector $\vec{k}_f$, the laws of conservation of energy and momentum must be satisfied. They read:
\begin{equation}
  E_f = E_i + \hbar\omega_0 , \qquad \vec{k}_f = \vec{k}_i + \vec{k}_{\text{ph}}.
  \label{eq:const}
\end{equation}

Using the parabolic band $E = \hbar^2 k^2 / 2m^\ast$ and the photon momentum $k_{\text{ph}} = \omega_0/c = 2\pi/\lambda_0$, equation~\eqref{eq:const} becomes:
\begin{equation}
  \frac{\hbar^2 k_f^2}{2m^\ast} = \frac{\hbar^2 k_i^2}{2m^\ast} + \hbar\omega_0 , \qquad k_f = k_i + \frac{2\pi}{\lambda_0}.
\end{equation}

The photon momentum is set by the wavelength alone. At $\lambda_0 = 1030~\mathrm{nm}$, $k_{\text{ph}} = 2\pi/\lambda_0 \approx 6.1\times10^{6}~\mathrm{m^{-1}}$. The electron momentum, on the other hand, is set by its kinetic energy in the conduction band. Taking a representative value $E_i \sim 1~\mathrm{eV}$, and any energy of order one eV leads to the same conclusion, we obtain:
\begin{equation}
  k_i = \frac{\sqrt{2 m^\ast E_i}}{\hbar} \approx 5\times10^{9}~\mathrm{m^{-1}}, \qquad \frac{k_{\text{ph}}}{k_i} \approx 10^{-3}.
\end{equation}

Conservation of momentum therefore forces $k_f \approx k_i$, hence $E_f \approx E_i$, which contradicts $E_f = E_i + \hbar\omega_0$ unless $\hbar\omega_0 \approx 0$.

The process becomes allowed if a third body carries away the momentum mismatch. In a polar dielectric such as $\mathrm{SiO_2}$, this third body is a phonon of wave vector $\vec{q}$ and energy $\hbar\omega_q$, so that:
\begin{equation}
  E_f = E_i + \hbar\omega_0 \pm \hbar\omega_q , \qquad \vec{k}_f = \vec{k}_i + \vec{k}_{\text{ph}} \pm \vec{q}.
\end{equation}

Since phonon wave vectors span the entire Brillouin zone:
$$q \lesssim \tfrac\pi a \sim 10^{10}~\mathrm{m^{-1}} \gtrsim k_i$$

Momentum can now be balanced, while $\hbar\omega_q \sim 0.06$--$0.15~\mathrm{eV} \ll \hbar\omega_0$ leaves the energy balance essentially unchanged. This phonon assisted mechanism is free carrier absorption (FCA), equivalently inverse Bremsstrahlung~\cite{mao2004, bulgakova2010}.

\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=1.5, >=stealth]

    % Axes (l'axe des abscisses est étendu vers la gauche)
    \draw[->, thick] (-4.5, 0) -- (4.5, 0) node[below right] {$k$};
    \draw[->, thick] (0, -0.5) -- (0, 4.5) node[above left] {$E$};

    % Parabolic curve (Conduction band)
    \draw[thick, blue, domain=-4:4, samples=100] plot (\x, {0.25*\x*\x});
    \node[blue, right] at (3.6, 4.1) {$E = \frac{\hbar^2 k^2}{2m^*}$};

    % Coordinate definitions (states)
    % Initial state I: k_i = 2, so E_i = 0.25 * (2)^2 = 1
    \coordinate (I) at (2, 1); 
    
    % Virtual state X: photon adds energy (vertical jump)
    \coordinate (X) at (2.2, 3.0625); 
    
    % Final state F1 (+q): phonon adds momentum (saut vers la droite)
    \coordinate (F1) at (3.7, 3.4225); 

    % Final state F2 (-q): phonon subtracts momentum (saut vers la gauche)
    \coordinate (F2) at (3.3, 2.7225); 

    % Dashed lines for axis projections
    \draw[dashed, gray] (I) -- (2, 0) node[below, text=black] {$k_i$};
    \draw[dashed, gray] (I) -- (0, 1) node[left, text=black] {$E_i$};
    \draw[dashed, gray] (F1) -- (3.7, 0) node[below, text=black] {$k_{f1}$};
    \draw[dashed, gray] (F2) -- (3.3, 0) node[below, text=black] {$k_{f2}$};
    \draw[dashed, gray] (F2) -- (F1); % Ligne horizontale traversant E_f
    \node[above left, text=black] at (0, 3.4225) {$E_{f1}$};
    \node[above left, text=black] at (0, 2.7225) {$E_{f2}$};
    
    % Transition arrows
    % 1. Transition due to Photon (Vertical energy jump)
    % Le label est déplacé à droite pour ne pas gêner la flèche -q
    \draw[dashed, gray] (0, 3.4225) -- (F1) node[left, text=black] {};
    \draw[dashed, gray] (0, 2.7225) -- (F2) node[left, text=black] {};
    \draw[->, thick, red] (I) -- (X) node[midway, left] {$\hbar\omega_0$ (Photon)};
    
    % 2. Transitions due to Phonon (+q and -q)
    \draw[->, thick, orange] (X) -- (F1) node[midway, above] {$+\vec{q}$};
    \draw[->, thick, orange] (X) -- (F2) node[near end, above] {$-\vec{q}$};

    % Points and state labels
    \filldraw[black] (I) circle (1.5pt) node[below right] {$(I)$ Initial};
    \filldraw[black] (F1) circle (1.5pt) node[above right] {$\quad(F_1)$ Final};
    \filldraw[black] (F2) circle (1.5pt) node[below right] {$\quad(F_2)$ Final};
    
    % Virtual state
    \filldraw[fill=white, draw=red, thick] (X) circle (1.5pt) node[above right, text=red] {$[X]$};

    % Summary box (déplacé en bas à gauche pour ne pas masquer la flèche -q)
    \node[draw, align=left, fill=white, rounded corners] at (-2.5, 1.5) {
        \textbf{Conservation}\\
        $E_f \approx E_i + \hbar\omega_0$\\
        $\vec{k}_f \approx \vec{k}_i \pm \vec{q}$
    };

\end{tikzpicture}
